newsitem.title: CANADA: Inco Ltd to resume talks with strikers.
newsitem.headline: Inco Ltd to resume talks with strikers.

text.p: Inco Ltd said on Thursday that it would resume talks at 1400 EDT/1800 GMT today with the union representing 4,670 striking workers at its Sudbury, Ontario mine operations.

"The decision to talk was only agreed to last evening," Inco spokesman David Allen told Reuters. "My expectation is that they'll talk probably through the weekend and at some point the union will come out of the talks and say, 'We have a package.'"
Inco's Sudbury workers, members of the United Steelworkers of America, Local 6500, went on strike at midnight on June 2, after voting 60.4 percent against a contract offer endorsed by union leaders.
According to Inco's 1997 production plan, the Ontario division was expected to produce about 230 million pounds of nickel, about 200 million pounds of copper and about four million pounds of cobalt.

Inco's Port Colborne, Ontario refinery, which processes cobalt, precious metals and electro-nickel, was not affected by the Sudbury strike. Unionized workers at the refinery approved the contract on June 2.
